title: Frequently asked questions
subtitle: Straight answers about this specific build, not general legal advice.
heroImageAlt: A pair of reading glasses resting on an open book.

items.question: Is this an official government site?
items.answerBody: No. This is an independent hackathon prototype, not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to the Government of India, the Ministry of Home Affairs, or the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre. If you need to report a real cybercrime, use the official portal at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.
items.linkLabel: See the full what's real vs mocked breakdown

items.question: Do I need to create an account to report?
items.answerBody: You sign in once with a number you already have, and you never upload an ID document or set a password. Signing in is what lets your details pre-fill and lets you see all your reports in one place.

items.question: Is my complaint here the same as filing an FIR?
items.answerBody: No. A complaint filed through this prototype, or through the real cybercrime.gov.in, is not an FIR. It's a cyber-crime complaint that can be forwarded to a bank for a freeze request and to a cyber cell for investigation. An FIR is a separate, formal criminal-procedure document filed at a police station; a cyber cell can advise on this, but this build does not create one.

items.question: What happens to my data?
items.answerBody: Only what's needed to process the report is collected: no Aadhaar, no PAN, no ID upload, no biometrics. What's stored, for how long, and who it's shared with is documented in full on the privacy page.

items.question: Is the OTP real?
items.answerBody: No, it's mocked. This prototype doesn't have a contract with an SMS gateway, so no message actually leaves the system; the code is shown directly on screen instead of being sent. The session and account mechanics behind it are built the same way a production system would be; only the delivery is simulated.
items.linkLabel: See what else is mocked vs real

items.question: What if I don't have all the details, like a transaction ID?
items.answerBody: You can still file. Every field beyond the essentials is optional: describe what happened in your own words and add whatever details you do have. You can always come back and add more later using your Complaint ID.

items.question: I already called 1930. Do I still need to file a report?
items.answerBody: Yes, and soon. The government's own guidance says that after calling 1930, completing the online report is mandatory within 24 hours of the call, or the bank-freeze request behind it can lapse. The real portal doesn't display this deadline anywhere; this build is telling you now so you don't lose the window.
